   1) INTRODUCTION


 a) Summary


                This document is the user manual for the Copernicus Marine Service global multi-
      year product GLOBAL_MULTIYEAR_WAV_001_032. It provides aggregated analyses from
      01/01/1980 to M-2, available on the Copernicus Marine Service server. The wave
      products are the integrated parameters computed from the total wave spectrum
       (significant wave height, period, direction, Stokes drift, ...etc), as well as the following
        partitions: the wind wave, the primary swell wave and the secondary swell wave.

        This product is global. It is defined on a standard grid at 1/5 degree (approx. 20 km).

      The product is organized in 3 datasets:
          - cmems_mod_glo_wav_my_0.2deg_PT3H-i containing 3-hourly instantaneous values
        for all the variables
          - cmems_mod_glo_wav_my_0.2deg-climatology_P1M-m containing monthly mean
      climatology values for sea surface wave significant height and sea surface wave mean
      period from variance spectral density second frequency moment on 1993-30/04/2019
       period.
          - cmems_mod_glo_wav_my_0.2deg_static containing the bathymetry

      The product is published on the Copernicus Marine Service dissemination server after
      automatic and human quality controls. Product is available on-line and disseminated
      through the Copernicus Marine Service Information System. Files downloaded are in
     NetCDF format and follow CF-1.6 convention.

      The analysis and forecasting system is described in the Quality Information Document
      (QUID – see in REFERENCES).

 b) Production System Description


           The global ocean reanalysis wave system of Météo-France (WAVERYS) with a
       resolution of 1/5° degree is providing analysis for the global ocean sea surface waves.
      The  initial time series starts on January 1st, 1980 and  is aggregated in time  until
     December 26th, 2018. This product includes 3-hourly instantaneous fields of integrated
     wave parameters from the total spectrum (significant height, period, direction, Stokes
         drift,  ...etc), as well as the following partitions: the wind wave, the primary and
      secondary swell waves


 Domain
  Resolution and grid                 GLOBAL (180°W-179.8°E ; 89.8°S – 89.8°N)
                                                 1/5º ; regular grid ; 1800 x 899

 Geographic coverage     This product is global with dedicated projection and spatial resolution.
                                                  It is defined on a standard collocated grid at 1/5 degree (approx. 20
                              km). The wave parameters are interpolated from the native grid
                           model, which is irregular with increasing distance in the latitudinal
                                                   direction close to the poles.





 Algorithm                   MFWAM (ECWAM-IFS-38R2 source code)

 Atmospheric forcings         ERA5 climatological winds and ice fraction: 3-hourly analysis

                       GLORYS12V1 current (GLOBAL_MULTIYEAR_PHY_001_030 Copernicus
 Current forcing
                                        Marine product): 3-hourly analysis

  Assimilation scheme                           Optimal interpolation

                               Significant wave height (SWH) from altimeters ERS1, TOPEX/POSEIDON,
  Assimilated observations     ERS2, GFO, Jason 2 & 3, Envisat, Saral, Cryosat-2 and Sentinel-3A;
                                              Sentinel-3 and Sentinel-1-SAR spectrum

  Initial conditions                               No

 Bathymetry                                   ETOPO2

     FAQ:

          1) The wave direction follows the classic meteorological convention: 0° north, 90°
              east, anti-trigonometric evolution, the direction indicates the direction of origin.
            NB: there is an offset of 180° in the netcdf attributes to take into account (netcdf
           compatible software normally takes it into account automatically).

          2) The wave spectra are not directly recorded along the model run because they
            are very heavy in terms of data (24 directions * 30 frequencies * all grid points *
            output time steps). Wave spectra are then lost during production, but they are
             nevertheless recorded at a few sporadic points for validation purposes. These
           few validation wave spectra are not disseminated within Copernicus Marine
              Service.



 c) Processing information

            1. Time coverage

     An archive of analysis since 1st January 1980 is available.

            2. Time averaging

      The fields are 3-hourly instantaneous at 00, 03, 06, 09, 12, 15, 18, 21 UTC.

   4) FILES NOMENCLATURE

        Information about nomenclature of files when downloaded can be found in this articles
        “ How is defined the nomenclature of Copernicus Marine data? | Copernicus Marine Help
       Center”

 a) Nomenclature of files when downloaded through the Copernicus Marine Service Web
     Portal Service

      Product files nomenclature when downloaded through the CMEMS MDS Services  is
     based on the following nomenclature:
      The scheme is: datasetname_nnnnnnnnnnnnn.nc
      where:
                  -  datasetname: as described previously
                  -  nnnnnnnnnnnnn: 13 digit integer corresponding to the current time (download
             time) in milliseconds since January 1, 1970 midnight UTC.
                  -   .nc: standard NetCDF filename extension.
                  -
      Example: cmems_mod_glo_wav_my_0.2deg_PT3H-i_1303461772348.nc

 b) Nomenclature of original files
      The scheme is: modelname_${date1}_R${date2}.nc
      where:
                  -  modelname: WAVERYS
                  -   date1: integer (format YYYYMMDD) corresponding to the field date
                  -   date2: integer (format YYYYMMDD) corresponding to the analysis date. In the
           case of GLOBAL_MULTIYEAR_WAV_001_032, date2 is equal to date1.
                  -   .nc: standard NetCDF filename extension.
                  -
      Example: WAVERYS_20180101_R20180101.nc (01/01/2018 field)

 c) Other information: mean centre of products, land mask value, missing value

      Real_Value = (Display_Value X scale_factor) + add_offset
      The missing value for this product is: -32767s
     Land mask are equal to “_FillValue” (see variable attribute on NetCDF file).
